import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# File paths for source tables
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_95/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_95/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_95/training_2.csv"

# Step 1: Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
df_source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df_source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)
df_source2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)

# Step 2: Understand the target schema and what columns are needed:
# Target schema: ['movie_id': int, 'title': str, 'F': float, 'M': float]
# From source0: movie_id, title (movie info)
# From source1: movie_id, user_id, rating (ratings)
# From source2: user_id, sex (user demographics)

# Step 3: Join source1 and source2 on user_id to get ratings with user sex
df_ratings_with_sex = pd.merge(df_source1, df_source2[['user_id', 'sex']], on='user_id', how='inner')

# Step 4: Aggregate ratings by movie_id and sex to get average rating per sex per movie
# We want columns F and M representing average rating by female and male users respectively
# Pivot or groupby with aggregation

# Group by movie_id and sex, calculate mean rating
grouped = df_ratings_with_sex.groupby(['movie_id', 'sex'])['rating'].mean().reset_index()

# Pivot to get columns 'F' and 'M'
pivot = grouped.pivot(index='movie_id', columns='sex', values='rating').rename(columns={'F': 'F', 'M': 'M'})

# Step 5: Join pivoted ratings with movie info (df_source0) on movie_id
# Keep only needed columns from df_source0: movie_id, title
df_movie_info = df_source0[['movie_id', 'title']]

# Merge movie info with pivoted ratings
df_target = pd.merge(df_movie_info, pivot, on='movie_id', how='left')

# Step 6: Ensure target schema and types
# movie_id: int
df_target['movie_id'] = df_target['movie_id'].astype(int)
# title: string
df_target['title'] = df_target['title'].astype(str)
# F and M: float (may have NaNs if no ratings from that sex)
df_target['F'] = df_target['F'].astype(float)
df_target['M'] = df_target['M'].astype(float)

# Step 7: Sort by movie_id for neatness (optional)
df_target = df_target.sort_values('movie_id').reset_index(drop=True)

# Step 8: Write the result to the specified path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_95/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source files with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_95/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_95/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_95/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source1 and Source2 on user_id
joined_user = pd.merge(source1, source2, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Compute average ratings by sex per movie_id
# Map sex to columns F and M with mean ratings
pivot = joined_user.pivot_table(index="movie_id", columns="sex", values="rating", aggfunc="mean").reset_index()
pivot = pivot.rename(columns={"F": "F", "M": "M"})

# Join Source0 (movie info) with pivot (average ratings by sex) on movie_id
joined_all = pd.merge(source0[["movie_id", "title"]], pivot, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Group by movie_id and title (primary key columns) and aggregate mean for F and M
result = joined_all.groupby(["movie_id", "title"], as_index=False).agg({"F": "mean", "M": "mean"})

# Write output with exact target schema and column order
result = result[["movie_id", "title", "F", "M"]]

result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_95/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
